title: Finite coefficient stages and their quotient arrows
statement: Let $\ell$ be prime and let $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ be a finite coefficient extension with its valuation ring and chosen uniformizer $t$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. A finite coefficient stage is a finite extension $F/\mathbf Q_\ell$, an embedding $\iota:E\hookrightarrow F$ over $\mathbf Q_\ell$, and a positive integer $n$. Its integer ring is $\mathcal O_F$, its parameter is $\iota(t)$, its ideal is $(\iota(t))^n$, and its ring is $\mathcal O_F/(\iota(t))^n$. The base stage uses $F=E$ and the identity embedding, so its quotient is canonically $\mathcal O_E/(t)^n$. An arrow from $(F,\iota,n)$ to $(H,\jmath,m)$ consists of an embedding $a:F\hookrightarrow H$ over $\mathbf Q_\ell$ satisfying $a\iota=\jmath$ and $m\le n$. Its coefficient homomorphism is the induced quotient map. Finite free for an arrow means that its target quotient is a finite and free module over its source quotient, using precisely that homomorphism. Identity and composite embeddings induce identity and composite quotient maps.
